overview.headline: Random mating as a Hardy Weinberg condition and assortative patterns in humans

keyPoints.point: Random mating is described as a condition of Hardy Weinberg Equilibrium that does not occur in humans
keyPoints.quote: random mating, a condition of HWE (Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium), does not occur

keyPoints.point: Random mating implies mating is arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered
keyPoints.quote: Random mating implies that mating should be arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered.

keyPoints.point: Humans tend to mate with similar individuals for visible traits such as height and ethnicity showing positive assortative mating
keyPoints.quote: humans tend to mate with individuals that are similar to themselves

keyPoints.point: Positive assortative mating increases homozygotes while negative assortative mating increases heterozygotes
keyPoints.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.

keyTerms.gloss: genetic equilibrium condition that assumes random mating to remain constant
keyTerms.quote: random mating, a condition of HWE (Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium), does not occur.

keyTerms.gloss: specific genomic position considered when assessing whether mating is arbitrary
keyTerms.quote: Random mating implies that mating should be arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered.

keyTerms.gloss: positive mating pattern where similar individuals mate non randomly and increase homozygotes
keyTerms.quote: This constitutes non-random, positive assortative mating.

keyTerms.gloss: mating between dissimilar genotypes that is described as more rare
keyTerms.quote: negative assortative mating is breeding between individuals with dissimilar genotypes, and is more rare.

keyTerms.gloss: individuals with identical alleles whose frequency shows an increase under positive assortative mating
keyTerms.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.

keyTerms.gloss: individuals with different alleles whose frequency shows an increase under negative assortative mating
keyTerms.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.
